verdicts.reason: A puts the can first and the headline below both the product and the badges, so the reading order is inverted. The badges are spread awkwardly far apart, the peach circle is cut off from the can it used to sit behind, the left-aligned headline clashes with the centred CTA, and the legal line is unreadably small. B puts the headline first but leaves huge dead gaps above and below the can, strands the badges below the CTA away from the product, mixes left-aligned copy with a centred can and CTA, and also has illegible legal text. A at least spaces things more evenly.

A has the badges orphaned below the CTA, cut off from the product, large dead areas around the can, mixed left and centred alignment, and illegible legal text. B follows a sensible order (headline, copy, product, badges with the product, centred CTA). Its flaws are the headline sitting on top of the decorative circle, a large empty gap between the copy and the can, a modest headline size and still-tiny legal text.

A uses arbitrary placements: the can is pushed right of centre, the CTA is pushed left, and the badges don't line up with the left margin of the copy. The headline also collides with the decorative circle, and the CTA reads as an afterthought. B (the same layout as pair 2's A) keeps the can and CTA on one shared centre line, but leaves the badges stranded under the CTA, has large dead zones and uses unreadably small legal text.
